First, I should understand what "self-sacrificing" means. It typically refers to an action where someone gives up their own interests or well-being for the benefit of others. So, if the King hung the prisoner in a tree as a self-sacrificing act, it would mean the King is doing something that might be harmful to himself but beneficial to others.

So, putting it all together, the King hanging the prisoner in a tree as a self-sacrificing act might not be morally acceptable.
